answer_2.quote: For QA-SRL and QANom evaluation, we adopt the measures put forward by . The unlabeled argument detection metric (UA) measures how many of the predicted answers are aligned with ground truth answers, based on token overlap. Aligned QAs are then inspected for question equivalence to assess semantic label assignment, comprising the labeled argument detection metric (LA).

answer_4.quote: We inspected the joint model predictions on the verbal and nominal QA-SRL test sets, taking samples of 50 QAs automatically classified as precision mistakes, and of 50 gold-standard QAs classified as recall misses (200 QAs total). Our findings are detailed in Appendix A.4.
answer_4.guideline: We judged whether precision mistakes were acceptable answers and whether recall mistakes had correct counterparts in model predictions, based on span-selection decisions and argument structure interpretations.
